question: Should OpenClaw expose a post-subagent-completion/pre-announcement plugin hook, and what child-run data plus announcement mutation authority may that hook receive?
rationale: The missing seam is source-proven, but choosing payload scope, delivery-status visibility, mutation/suppression semantics, ordering, and plugin trust boundaries creates public API and security behavior that automation should not decide.

options.title: Generic Output/Delivery Boundary
options.body: Design one typed output or delivery review boundary that covers subagent completions with explicit redaction, suppression, and delivery-result semantics instead of adding an ad hoc subagent-only interceptor.

options.title: Observation-Only Subagent Event
options.body: Expose a narrow post-completion event with metadata and delivery status only, leaving announcement mutation and suppression to existing or future delivery policy surfaces.

options.title: Keep Existing Hooks Only
options.body: Decline the new core hook for now and document how plugins should combine subagent_ended, message_sent, and delivery policy workarounds until a stronger consumer appears.

recommendation.title: Generic Output/Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Design one typed output or delivery review boundary that covers subagent completions with explicit redaction, suppression, and delivery-result semantics instead of adding an ad hoc subagent-only interceptor.
